recipes.name: Winter Lentil Vegetable Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 (28 ounce) can whole peeled tomatoes, chopped

steps.text: Place the lentils into a stockpot or a Dutch oven and add water to twice the depth of the lentils. Bring to a boil, then lower heat and let simmer for about 15 minutes. Drain and rinse lentils; return them to the pot.

Add onion, celery, cabbage, tomatoes, chicken broth, carrots and garlic to the pot and season with salt, pepper, sugar, basil, thyme and curry. Cook, simmering for 1 1/2 to 2 hours or until desired tenderness is achieved.

raw_recipe.headline: Winter Lentil Vegetable Soup
raw_recipe.description: This soup has very little fat, is cheap and easy to make and delicious. Our family practically lives on it in the winter and I usually double the recipe. Sprinkle grated cheddar on top if you wish. If you can't hang around long enough for this to cook, put it in a slow cooker.

review.reviewBody: I found this to be a very good soup. However, I made a few changes because I wanted to make a lot. So I used 1 1/2 cups Lentils, 3 celery, 2 garlic cloves, added 2 14 oz cans of petite diced tomato's with Jalapeno's for some zest, a whole head of cabbage, 6 carrots, 5 cups of organic free-range chicken broth, and 4 cups of water. I dbl'd the spices and added a Greek-Allspice. I ended up with a big, delicious, pot of Lentil's and veggi's. Wonderful, healthy, and low in fat. Cant go wrong with that!!!!
This soup came out great. I cooked this in the crockpot instead and I added a chicken bouillon cube. I also sautéed the onion and some minced garlic on the stovetop first to enhance the flavor.

I cooked this in my crockpot on high for about 3 hours. I don't like cooked tomatoes so I subbed 1 diced sweet potato. I had a cabbage but really needed to use up my bag of coleslaw which was so much easier too! I found the soup to be bland and had to add more of the spices. We still felt like the soup was lacking, so I diced up 1 link of beef sausage & cooked it on the stovetop, then adding to crockpot. The sausage really brought the soup together for us and now I will definatly make it again.

Made some changes simply because I didn’t have all the ingredients on hand, but it was a wonderful, warm winter soup/stew. Will definitely make it again. 

After reading other reviews, I did double the stock (4 C) and used red potatoes (instead of cabbage). I also added fennel seeds and fresh chopped anise (didn’t have celery). To round it out I added a couple cups of spinach with 10 minutes left. Good base recipe.

This soup was easy to throw together and very good. I made mine in the slow cooker. At the advice of others I used the coleslaw mix. I didn't have any basil on hand, so I used canned stewed Italian style tomatoes and chopped them. For lentils I used a mix of red and yellow. I did find I had to add a bit extra broth and cooking time was around 7 hrs on low to fully cook the yellow lentil. Will definitely keep this as a staple!

Fantastic! I converted for vegan. Vegetable not chicken broth, half the salt and pepper, 1 1/2 cloves garlic, 1/2 cup onion, maple syrup not white sugar, added a bay leaf and a scrubbed medium potato cut into small cubes. I had a leek in the fridge so I chopped it up and included it. Fried the garlic and onion in a little veggie broth before throwing it in. One of the cans of chopped tomatoes was basil garlic and oregano.
There is plenty of salt in the broth and the canned tomatoes. I will forego adding salt next time. At serving time offer cajun seasoning and cayenne pepper at the table for more bite.
Made this last night. Very good. I didn't precook the lentils. I put everything in my presser cooker and cooked it for 7 min. Turned out perfect. Added some frozen peas when it was done. Was a hit.

As written, 3 stars. Embellished, 4 stars. It's a great starting off recipe. I sautéed the veggies, except for the cabbage, in olive oil, then added about 5 cups of homemade veggie stock, tomatoes, lentils and cabbage and nearly tripled the spices including lots of black garlic pepper and simmered everything for about an hour. It was really good. Better the next day and freezes well.

I made this in an Instant Pot in less than 30 minutes. Added a couple frozen chicken breasts, full cup of lentils, can of Rotel, can of water, little salt and plenty black pepper. AWESOME! This is a keeper.

This is a great soup. I made a few alterations..I added smoked turkey sausage, 2 14 oz cans of diced tomoatoes (one was fire roasted), and extra chicken stock and water. I also sauteed the onions, carrots and celery and I did not precook the lentils as other reviewers had suggested..I cooked about 8 hrs in crockpot and it turned out great! The house smelled great too.

Tasty and forgiving recipe...alot going on with baby needs/care while making recipe so looked at it and then "went from memory" sat down to look at recipe afterwards and realized my memory wasn't particularly accurate; Here's what I had done: threw 1.5 onions in food processor then into pan with olive oil, tumeric/salt stirred/let cook; carrots in food processor then into pan; yogurt container of frozen purreed tomatoes in and one box of chicken broth then put lid on kept stirring and breaking chunk apart; added rinsed lentils; garlic powder, marjorum, thyme, black pepper, more salt, curry powder, green beans that snapped ends off of and threw in food processor for moment; kept stirring and boiling/simmering; added some red quinoa for lastish 15 minutes after rinsing it; added pumpkin puree from refrig from pumpkin that had roasted previously. Cooked till tasted ready; served with corn bread and cheese- we enjoyed enough that I took the time to think back on what had done cause my husband wanted me to make it again sometime...
Allrecipes are good, straight forward recipes. I added a diced potato to this recipe. I didn't have curry, so I used cumin and chapotle. This is a good, basic recipe.

Really liked this, and really like the nutritional breakdown. I tasted it right after it started to simmer and felt that it needed more seasoning. I increased all of the seasoning ingredients, but didn’t add any new. Also, it was very thick, and it’ll only become thicker as it simmers and cooks down stove top for a couple hours, so be prepared to add more liquid (chicken broth, V8 juice, water, your choice). After 2 hours, both the celery and carrot still had a little bit of a bite, but I’d prefer that over mushy veggies. I did add one thing, a handful of frozen peas, and that gave this soup a nice pop of color. I know I’ll add more lentils next time, because they were a bit lost.

What a fabulous soup. Followed as is except I omitted thyme as I don’t like it and used 3 cups of broth. The next time I make it I’m going to throw the lentils in with everything and cook it that way. I don’t see the use of the extra step of cooking the lentils separately.
This is a great recipe. I love it!
Very nice. Easy to make and it is a flexible recipe. Like some other folks here I altered the ingredients a little (used veg broth to make a vegan version). Good with fresh bread
a little bland - needs more salt - pretty easy and i used thawed frozen spinach - substituted chicken broth for water

I made an account on here just to review this recipe. Allrecipes has a tendency to frustrate me since the reviews don’t usually accurately reflect the recipe as written. This recipe however, AS WRITTEN, is Delicious. I followed it to a T and I’m back on here to make it again as part of my second week of meal prep. So easy and delicious.
This was super easy to make and easily modified to the InstaPot. Approved in 1 cup serving size for post-bariatric surgery.

Fresh, delicious, comforting and filling in a cold day. I followed the recipe but subbed a can of petite diced tomatoes, used 4 cups of chicken broth and added a dash of cumin. Great recipe! Thank you :)
